cap: Ten steps from setup to closeout. Find a tool, fold sections, ↺ Show all tools.
text: The menu on the left follows a job from start to finish, in ten numbered steps, from project setup to reports and closeout. Tools and reference, your projects and User Settings sit below, ready any time. Tap a heading to fold a section. Type in Find a tool to jump straight to a page. If any tools are hidden, Show all tools at the top brings every one back.

cap: Page help, Guide me, the i beside each value, and Clear all fields with Undo.
text: Every page has Page help, and Guide me, which walks you through the page one step at a time. The small i beside each value explains it in plain English, with its unit, the normal range and the industry default. Clear all fields starts one page over, after asking first. Undo puts it back. What's new lists the tools added in each version.

cap: Project name, client and site address. The address picks the codes.
text: Step one is Company and Project. Name the project, enter the client, and type the site address. The state and county fill in from the address, and they choose which codes apply. Pick feet or meters. Your company details are saved once and fill in every new project. Required boxes are marked, and reports warn you if one is empty.

cap: Pick the main system and the others on the job. The menu follows your pick.
text: On Project Systems and Toolkits, pick the main system, such as fire alarm, access control or emergency responder radio, and tick any other systems on the same job. Each one brings its own toolkit: design pages, install steps, tests, repairs and maintenance. The menu follows your pick, showing the tools the job needs and hiding the rest. Custom lets you choose every page yourself.

cap: An address or GPS point on the map and in 3D, then a starting plan in one tap.
text: Find Location and Auto-Plan takes an address or G P S coordinates, with suggestions as you type, and shows the spot on topo maps, satellite pictures and in three D, with its ground height. Tap Build plan for this location, and the app looks over the terrain for a good tower spot nearby, sets up the sites, and gives you a complete starting plan to review.

cap: Each site's position, ground height, structure and antenna, and runs between sites.
text: Site Data and G P S holds each site: its position, ground height, structure and antenna height. It shows the distance and azimuth between sites, and the existing towers nearby. Use this device's G P S, a G P S receiver, or bring in a spreadsheet of sites. Runs between sites plan fiber, copper, power or conduit, measured over the real terrain.

cap: Notes, photos and GPS points, with the site survey checklist.
text: Step two is the site survey. On Field Notes and Photos, write a note, take photos with the camera, and save your G P S position with each one. The site survey checklist keeps track of what to look at while you are there, and checks off as you go. Notes and photos are kept with the project, and print in the site survey report.

cap: Photos around a spot, lined up with the terrain, towers and blocked views marked.
text: On Photo Site Survey, stand where an antenna might go and take photos all the way around. The app reads the G P S and compass direction in each photo, lines them up into one panorama, and fits the skyline to the terrain. Project sites and nearby towers show their distance and whether a ridge hides them. Save the picture, and it prints in the report.

cap: Topo and satellite maps, 3D tilt view, measuring, drawn lines and full page.
text: Map and Terrain shows your sites on topo maps or satellite pictures. Zoom in up close for street-level detail. Three D tilt view turns the map into a model of the ground, and checks line of sight on each hop. Measure gives distance and azimuth. Drawn lines show the predicted signal along a road or cable route. Full page adds layers, zoom and tilt buttons.

cap: Wi-Fi scans placed on the floor plan become signal, noise and channel heat maps.
text: Wi-Fi and Network Survey turns Wi-Fi readings into heat maps on the floor plan. Load the plan and its size, walk the space, and at each stop tap your spot and paste a scan from the laptop, or import a survey app's file. The app maps the signal, noise, signal to noise ratio, channels and access points, so weak spots and overlaps are easy to see.

cap: A meter or the phone, readings saved with GPS, compared with the prediction.
text: On Live Signal Readings, connect a signal meter by Bluetooth, a U S B cable or Wi-Fi, or use the phone's own signal. Save a reading, or let it save every few seconds as you walk, each with its G P S position. Files from phone apps and meters come in too. The app compares the readings with the prediction and runs the indoor grid test floor by floor.

cap: Ten or more field readings tune the prediction to the real site.
text: Drive Test and Calibration brings the field readings together with the prediction. Each reading is matched to the predicted signal at the same spot, on the map and in a table. With ten or more readings, the app tunes the prediction model to the real site, and shows how far off it was before and after. Every coverage map then uses the tuning.

cap: Drop in a PDF, DXF or picture; get a graded, true-scale plan and 3D model.
text: Step three is low-voltage design, and it starts with the floor plan. Drop a P D F, D X F or picture onto Floor Plan to two D and three D. The app reads the scale, traces the walls, doors, windows and rooms, and grades the result. A poor file gets a list of problems and fixes. Add the plan to the project, and every design page uses it.

cap: Describe the building; get the devices for each system, laid out in 2D and 3D.
text: On Auto-Design, describe the building: its type, floors, size, rooms and doors. The app recommends the devices for each system on the job, such as smoke detectors, horn strobes, cameras, card readers and access points, lays them out, and shows them on a two D plan and a three D model. Change the building, and the layout updates right away.

cap: Building materials, every system on its own layers, true-scale plan and 3D.
text: Two D and three D Models with Layers shows every system on the job. Pick what the building is made of, and each material shows the radio signal it costs. The plan is drawn to true scale, with layers for devices, coverage, cable runs and heat maps. Tap Only this to see one system. The results show signal loss, echo, firestops and fire ratings.

cap: Several buildings, linked by fiber, copper, conduit or wireless bridges.
text: Multi-Building Site and Campus handles a site with several buildings. Add each building with its own type, floors and materials, and link them with underground or aerial fiber, copper, empty conduit, or a wireless bridge, which gets its own signal check. The site plan and three D model show the whole campus, and the cable schedule and materials add up every building and link.

cap: NFPA 72 standby battery, NAC voltage drop and NEC 760 checks.
text: Fire Alarm and Batteries sizes the standby battery for twenty-four hours of standby and five minutes of alarm, or fifteen for mass notification, with a safety factor. It checks the voltage drop on each notification circuit to the last device. Change the wire gauge or length, and the end-of-line voltage updates. The NFPA seventy-two and N E C checks run as you type.

cap: Siren database, coverage circles on the map, codes by address, and test schedules.
text: Outdoor Warning Sirens plans tornado, flood and plant warning sirens. Pick a model from the built-in siren database, current or legacy, and tap the map to place it. Each circle shows where that siren is loud enough over the background noise, using FEMA's planning guide. The federal, state and local codes load from the project address, and the siren tests go straight into Final Testing.

cap: Donor signal, BDA gain and downlink budget, IFC and NFPA 1225 checks, booster registration.
text: Emergency Radio covers E R C E S and B D A systems. It works out the donor signal, the B D A gain and the downlink budget to the worst spot in the building, against minus ninety-five dB m on ninety percent of each floor. The I F C and NFPA twelve twenty-five checks run live, the donor card shows where to aim, and the F C C booster registration fills in.

cap: Draw walls, place antennas, see the multi-wall heat map in 2D or 3D.
text: Indoor Coverage and DAS lets you draw the walls on a floor plan, pick what each wall is made of, and place DAS antennas or access points. The multi-wall model shows the coverage right away as a heat map. Drywall costs about two decibels, concrete block ten, and low-E glass about twenty. Switch to three D walls to see the floor from any angle.

cap: Speakers and horns on the floor plan: sound level and speech clarity maps, codes and tests.
text: Indoor Coverage also plans sound. Switch the plan to Sound, and place paging speakers, voice evacuation speakers or fire alarm horns on the same floor plan and walls. The heat map shows the sound level, or the speech clarity score, room by room, with plain advice on what to change. The NFPA seventy-two edition your state adopted loads by itself, and outdoor sirens show how loud they are inside.

cap: Loads, battery bank, solar array and wire sizes, with NEC 690 checks.
text: Solar and DC Power sizes power for a remote site, such as a radio repeater or an emergency call box. List the loads and hours, choose the days of battery backup, and the app sizes the battery bank, the solar array, using the worst month of sun for your location, and the wire sizes. The N E C six ninety checks cover string voltage and conductors.

cap: Ground rods, bonding, surge protection and structure class, with live code checks.
text: Grounding and Structure covers the grounding electrode system: ground rods, the ground ring, bonding conductors and surge protection, with live checks against the N E C, such as eight-foot rods at least six feet apart, and ten gauge copper bonding. It also sets the structure class for the tower or mast, so the loading and the code checks match the site.

cap: A county's frequencies, trunked sites and talkgroups, kept encrypted on this device.
text: Step four is radio design. Radio Reference Frequencies uses your Premium login to download a county's frequencies, trunked sites and talkgroups while you are online, for fire, police, E M S and other users. They are protected information, so they stay encrypted on this device only, and work offline. They feed the emergency radio and B D A pages.

cap: Registered towers and licensed transmitters nearby, who is on each, on what frequencies.
text: F C C Towers and Licenses lists every registered tower and licensed transmitter around a site, an address or your G P S. Each tower shows the owner, the height, the distance and the azimuth. Open one to see who is on it and on what frequencies. Narrow the list by band or kind of user. The data for five states is built in, so it works offline.

cap: Band, radio, antenna and coax: EIRP, ERP and maximum allowable path loss.
text: Equipment and Link Budget picks the band, the radio, the antennas, and the coax with its length. The app works out the feeder loss from the datasheet, the E I R P and E R P, and the maximum allowable path loss, after margins for fading, body loss and building penetration. That number tells you how far the signal can reach before it falls below the receiver's sensitivity.

cap: Ground between two sites, earth curve, line of sight and 60 % Fresnel clearance.
text: Path Profile shows the ground between two sites, with the earth's curve, the line of sight and the first Fresnel zone, and tells you if sixty percent of it is clear. For example, a five point eight gigahertz link over ten miles loses about one hundred thirty-two decibels, and needs about twenty-eight feet of clearance at mid-path. Trees and buildings can be added as clutter.

cap: A signal heat map over the terrain, checked against your acceptance criteria.
text: Coverage Prediction paints a signal heat map over the terrain, using Okumura-Hata or COST two thirty-one with terrain diffraction, and any tuning from your drive test. It checks the result against your acceptance criteria for mobile, portable and in-building radios, and shows the percent of the area that passes. Export the map for Google Earth or G I S, or save it as a scenario.

cap: Drop a pin with a reading on any heat map. The app checks the balance and says what to change.
text: Reading pins work on every heat map: coverage, drive tests, scenarios, the building models, the campus, and indoor radio and sound. Tap Drop a reading pin, touch the map, and type what your meter read, or pin your G P S position. The app compares each pin with the prediction and the target, and recommends what to change, such as raising the power, moving an antenna, or adding one.

cap: Where the main beam lands, a recommended downtilt, and a true-scale side view.
text: Tilt, Azimuth and Power shapes the footprint. It shows where the main beam and its edges land on the ground, and recommends a downtilt for your target radius. The side view follows the real ground along the antenna's azimuth, in true scale or with the heights stretched, and the three D view shows the beam as a wedge over the terrain.

cap: Best server, overlap, and co-channel and adjacent-channel interference across sites.
text: Multi-site and Interference runs every transmitting site together on one grid, with the same model and terrain as the coverage page. It maps the best server at each spot, how many sites overlap, and the carrier to interference ratio from co-channel and adjacent-channel signals. That shows where simulcast sites help, and where two transmitters on nearby channels will fight each other.

cap: Saved coverage runs side by side: inputs changed, area gained and lost, difference map.
text: Scenarios and Compare keeps each coverage run you save, with every input behind it. Pick a baseline and a comparison, and the app shows which inputs changed, how each acceptance result moved, the area gained and lost at each signal level, and a difference map. Restore inputs puts a scenario's radio settings back into the project. Export the comparison for the report.

cap: Terrain, your towers, existing towers and the Fresnel zone in 3D.
text: Three D Model shows the terrain with your towers, the radio path and the first Fresnel zone. Drag to turn it, and stretch the heights to read the ground. Existing towers and masts nearby stand up with their names and heights, so you can plan around them or look for a place to co-locate. Terrain and towers download by themselves and work offline.

cap: Antenna sizes, ground wave and sky wave, MUF and NVIS.
text: L F and H F Systems covers long-range radio. It sizes dipoles and monopoles and their ground systems, predicts ground wave field strength over sea water, farmland or rock, and works out sky wave: the highest usable frequency and near vertical paths for a given distance. For example, one kilowatt at one point seven megahertz carries much farther over sea water than over dry rock.

cap: Every check from every page in one list, with the code section and the fix.
text: Step five is codes, permits and drawings. Code Compliance shows the codes in force for the project address, and every check from every page in one list. Each finding is a violation, a warning or a note, cites the code and section in the edition your state has adopted, and gives a recommended fix. Tap a finding to open the page where you fix it.

cap: Does a tower, mast or antenna need FAA notice? Airports built in, works offline.
text: The F A A Height Check tells you if a new tower, mast or antenna needs F A A notice. Pick the location and type the overall height, to the very top. The ground height fills in, and the app checks every airport and heliport nearby against the federal rules, and shows the tallest structure you can build without filing. The airports are built in, so it works offline.

cap: Cover sheet, floor plans per system, riser and schedules, at standard scales, with CAD export.
text: Blueprints and Drawing Sets turns the design into a permit and shop drawing set: a cover sheet with the codes and a sheet index, a floor plan for each system, a riser diagram and schedules. Choose the sheet size and an architectural scale, add your title block, and print it, save it as P D F, or export it for CAD.

cap: Equipment for every system, legacy models, manuals and official recalls.
text: Step six is equipment and materials. The Specifications Library covers every low-voltage system, from fire alarm panels to card readers, cameras and antennas. Legacy equipment lists older models you still find on service calls, with suggested replacements and repair notes. Attach manuals to keep them on this device. Official recalls are built in, and any match in a project is flagged on every page.

cap: Equipment and materials with unit costs, labor, tax, markup and budgets.
text: The Materials List and Estimate adds up the equipment and materials for the job. Type a unit cost, and the totals fill in. Change or remove any line, and search for parts online at the suppliers you pick. Suggest labor gives a starting set of hours from the materials. Add tax, shipping and markup, and anything over budget shows in red before you order.

cap: Your suppliers, with contacts, accounts and terms, and live stock where offered.
text: The Vendors page keeps your suppliers in one place: the sales rep, phone, email, account number and terms. Add a field for anything else you track. Pick a vendor on any line of the materials list. If a vendor offers a stock address, the app checks stock and price by itself when you are online, so you know what is on the shelf.

cap: Step-by-step guides with color wiring diagrams, tools, safety notes and tests.
text: Step seven is installation. Installation Guides has a guide for each kind of install, with this project's systems listed first. Each guide has a color wiring diagram, the tools, safety notes, numbered steps, the tests for closeout and the code articles that apply. The diagrams use the antenna and coax chosen in the project. Print a copy for the crew.

cap: Acceptance tests with expected values, measured results and pass or fail.
text: Step eight is testing. Final Testing loads the standard acceptance tests for the job: coax sweeps and distance to fault, P I M, ground resistance, bonding, transmit power and frequency, antenna aim, the drive test, the E R C E S grid test and the battery run test. Type each result as you go. Pass or fail shows right away, and it all prints in the commissioning report.

cap: Maintenance intervals, common faults and fixes, test steps, standards and manuals.
text: Step nine is service and repair. Service and Maintenance Resources is the reference shelf for each system: what to inspect or test and how often, with the code reference, the common faults and their fixes, the test and inspection steps, and the standards. Find online opens service manuals, troubleshooting guides and how-to videos for the equipment.

cap: Pick the system, the equipment and the problem; get checks with the values to expect.
text: The Troubleshooting Wizard works in short steps. Pick the system, then the equipment, such as a smoke detector, a mag lock, a camera or a B D A, then what is wrong. The app lists the likely causes in order, how to test each one, and the value to expect on the meter, so you check the most likely fault first.

cap: Scan a tag to open a device: serial, location, warranty and maintenance due.
text: Equipment and Asset Tags keeps track of every device. Tap Scan tag and point the camera at a barcode or Q R code. A new tag starts a new device, and a tag you already have opens it. Keep the make, model, serial number, location, photos, install date, warranty and maintenance schedule. The list shows what is due, and prints Q R labels.

cap: The finished project, filled in live: title block, sheets, plans, model and schedules.
text: Step ten is reports and closeout. Project Build Output shows the finished project as it is built: the title block, the sheet index, the floor plans with layers, the three D model, the schedules, and what was added when. It updates by itself as you work on any page, and every missing item links to the page where you add it.

cap: Proposals, build plans, survey reports and the closeout package. Then mark the project complete.
text: Reports, Proposals and Closeout builds the proposal, the build plan, the site survey report or the closeout package. Choose the sections, then print it, or save it as P D F, Word or Excel. When the job is done, tap Mark project complete. The date is saved with the project, and the menu goes back to the default view, ready for the next job.

cap: Cabling, power, fire alarm, sound and radio calculators, with Apply to fields.
text: Now the tools, which you can open any time. Calculators covers cabling, power, fire alarm, sound, radio and antennas, such as the azimuth calculator between two G P S points. Each calculator keeps its own numbers, and shows the site conditions that change its result, like a cold forecast. Apply to fields copies a result into the project, with Undo right there.

cap: Signal meters, GPS receivers, laser meters and barcode scanners, connected once.
text: Bluetooth and Wi-Fi Devices connects your equipment once, and every page uses it. Connect a signal meter, a G P S receiver, a laser distance meter or a barcode scanner, by Bluetooth, a U S B cable, or Wi-Fi on the local network. A laser measurement goes right into the box you tap, and every G P S button uses the receiver.

cap: A USB receiver as a spectrum analyzer: markers, waterfall, BDA tests, signed reports.
text: The R F Spectrum Analyzer turns a U S B receiver, such as a tiny S A, an R T L S D R or a Hack R F, into a spectrum analyzer. Markers, max hold, the waterfall, channel power and occupied bandwidth work like a bench analyzer. Guided tests check B D A noise and the donor signal, and the certification tests save a signed report.

cap: Calibrated sound levels, 1/3-octave analyzer, RT60, STI and NFPA 72 audibility.
text: The Audio and Acoustic Analyzer is a sound level meter and real-time analyzer. Calibrate with a ninety-four dB calibrator, load the microphone's calibration file, and read dB S P L with A, C or Z weighting. A sine sweep measures the room's reverberation and speech intelligibility, and the fire alarm audibility test saves a signed report.

cap: The job site on a map, with directions in Google Maps, Apple Maps or Waze.
text: Map and Directions shows the project site on a map, with the client contact for the crew. One tap opens turn-by-turn directions in Google Maps, Apple Maps or Waze, from where you are or from your office. Show me on the map adds your position and the distance and direction to the site. Copy the address or G P S to send it on.

cap: Fire marshals, inspectors and licensing boards by state, county and city.
text: Contacts and Web Resources lists the fire marshals, building inspectors, code offices and licensing boards for the state, county and city, or by ZIP code. Tap a phone number to call, or an address to open the map. The web resources tab has code pages and other links. Add, edit or remove your own contacts too.

cap: Live radar, alerts and the 7-day forecast for the job, with work-day checks.
text: Weather and Radar shows live N O A A radar, alerts, current conditions and the seven-day forecast for the job site, or for where you are. The work-day checks flag wind, storms, heat and cold for jobs like tower climbing or lift work. The latest download is saved, so the last forecast is still there when you lose signal.

cap: Declination at the job, how it changes, and NOAA's space weather forecast.
text: Magnetic Field and Space Weather shows how far a compass points away from true north at the job, from N O A A's magnetic model, and how that changes over the years. Every azimuth in the app uses it. The space weather forecast warns of geomagnetic storms and radio blackouts that can upset G P S and H F radio.

cap: Satellite pictures, topo maps and terrain for a whole job area, before you lose signal.
text: Offline Map Packs saves satellite pictures, topo maps and terrain for a whole job area before you go where there is no signal. Choose the area, around your sites or an address, and the level of detail. You see the size before you download, then the progress, and every pack you saved. Terrain is what path profiles, coverage and three D need.

cap: A reading guide from electrical basics to RF engineering, with best practices.
text: Low-Voltage and R F Design Principles is a built-in reading guide, from Ohm's law and cabling to grounding, each system, and troubleshooting. Part six covers R F engineering: decibels, antennas, propagation, Fresnel zones, fading, noise and interference. Part seven covers design concepts. Each section ends with industry best practices, and the index finds any topic.

cap: Every project saved on this device, with history, backups and automatic care.
text: Projects and Storage keeps every project on this device, saved as you work, with its history and daily backups. Open, copy or delete a project here. Automatic care checks each saved copy and puts back the last good version if one is ever damaged, keeps downloaded data current, and checks for app updates by itself.

cap: Optional sign-in: private accounts, fingerprint or face, recovery code, and sharing.
text: Users and Sign-in is off until you turn it on. Then each person signs in with a PIN, a password, or a fingerprint or face, and their projects are locked with their own key, so nobody else can open them. Write down the recovery code: it resets a forgotten PIN. To work together, share a project with another user, or save a locked copy to send.

cap: Phone, tablet and computer kept in step: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, email or a cloud folder.
text: Sync Devices keeps your phone, tablet and computer in step. Every device has a full copy and works offline. Sync directly over Wi-Fi by scanning a code, by Bluetooth or email, or through a cloud-drive folder. Copies are merged part by part, with the newest change winning, so work from the field and the office comes together.

cap: Turn tools on or off, check the whole project, and keep app keys.
text: In User Settings, untick the tools you don't use, and they leave the menu. Nothing is deleted, and Show all tools brings them back. Check my data goes through the whole project for empty, out of range or mismatched values, with a fix for each. The Radio Reference app key is typed here once, and kept encrypted.
